subject: maths
pattern: Three Dimensional Geometry appears for 6-9 marks: 1-mark direction cosines/ratios, 2-3 mark numericals (angle between lines, distance of a point from a plane, equation of plane or line) and a 5-mark question on shortest distance between skew lines or plane equation. Quote the vector formula first, then substitute carefully.

questions.q: Write the direction cosines of the x-axis.
questions.answer: The x-axis makes angles $0^\circ,90^\circ,90^\circ$ with the axes, so direction cosines are $\cos0^\circ,\cos90^\circ,\cos90^\circ=1,0,0$.

questions.q: If a line has direction ratios $2,3,-6$, find its direction cosines.
keywords: divide by root of sum of squares

questions.q: Write the vector equation of the line passing through a point with position vector $\vec a$ and parallel to the vector $\vec b$.
questions.answer: $\vec r=\vec a+\lambda\vec b$, where $\lambda$ is a scalar parameter.

questions.q: Find the direction cosines of the line joining the points $(-2,4,-5)$ and $(1,2,3)$.
Find the angle between the lines whose direction ratios are $1,1,2$ and $\sqrt3-1,-\sqrt3-1,4$.
Find the distance of the point $(2,5,-3)$ from the plane $\vec r\cdot(6\hat i-3\hat j+2\hat k)=5$.
Find the shortest distance between the lines $\vec r=(\hat i+2\hat j+3\hat k)+\lambda(\hat i-3\hat j+2\hat k)$ and $\vec r=(4\hat i+5\hat j+6\hat k)+\mu(2\hat i+3\hat j+\hat k)$.
questions.answer: $\vec a_2-\vec a_1=3\hat i+3\hat j+3\hat k$. $\vec b_1\times\vec b_2=-9\hat i+3\hat j+9\hat k$, magnitude $\sqrt{171}=3\sqrt{19}$. $(\vec a_2-\vec a_1)\cdot(\vec b_1\times\vec b_2)=-27+9+27=9$. $d=\frac{9}{3\sqrt{19}}=\frac{3}{\sqrt{19}}$ units.

questions.q: Find the equation of the plane passing through the points $(1,1,0)$, $(1,2,1)$ and $(-2,2,-1)$.
questions.answer: $\vec{AB}=(0,1,1)$, $\vec{AC}=(-3,1,-1)$. Normal $=\vec{AB}\times\vec{AC}=-2\hat i-3\hat j+3\hat k$. Plane: $-2(x-1)-3(y-1)+3z=0\Rightarrow2x+3y-3z=5$. (Check: both other points satisfy it.)

questions.q: Find the vector and Cartesian equations of the line through $(5,2,-4)$ and parallel to the vector $3\hat i+2\hat j-8\hat k$.
questions.answer: Vector form: $\vec r=(5\hat i+2\hat j-4\hat k)+\lambda(3\hat i+2\hat j-8\hat k)$. Cartesian form: $\frac{x-5}{3}=\frac{y-2}{2}=\frac{z+4}{-8}$.

questions.q: Find the angle between the line $\dfrac{x+3}{3}=\dfrac{y-1}{5}=\dfrac{z+3}{4}$ and the plane $10x+2y-11z=3$.
questions.answer: Line direction $\vec b=(3,5,4)$, plane normal $\vec n=(10,2,-11)$. $\sin\theta=\frac{|\vec b\cdot\vec n|}{|\vec b||\vec n|}=\frac{|30+10-44|}{5\sqrt2\cdot15}=\frac{4}{75\sqrt2}=\frac{2\sqrt2}{75}$. $\theta=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{2\sqrt2}{75}\right)$.

questions.q: Derive the formula for the shortest distance between two skew lines $\vec r=\vec a_1+\lambda\vec b_1$ and $\vec r=\vec a_2+\mu\vec b_2$.
questions.answer: Let $P(\vec a_1)$ and $Q(\vec a_2)$ be points on the lines. The shortest distance is along the common perpendicular, direction $\vec b_1\times\vec b_2$. Shortest distance $=$ projection of $\vec{PQ}=\vec a_2-\vec a_1$ on $\vec b_1\times\vec b_2$. Unit normal $\hat n=\frac{\vec b_1\times\vec b_2}{|\vec b_1\times\vec b_2|}$, so $d=|(\vec a_2-\vec a_1)\cdot\hat n|=\frac{|(\vec a_2-\vec a_1)\cdot(\vec b_1\times\vec b_2)|}{|\vec b_1\times\vec b_2|}$. [Diagram: two skew lines with PQ and common perpendicular.]

questions.q: Derive the vector equation of a plane in normal form $\vec r\cdot\hat n=d$ and deduce the Cartesian form $lx+my+nz=d$.
questions.answer: Let the perpendicular from the origin to the plane meet it at $N$, $\vec{ON}=d\hat n$ with $d>0$. For any point $P$ on the plane with $\vec{OP}=\vec r$, $\vec{NP}=\vec r-d\hat n$ is perpendicular to $\hat n$. So $(\vec r-d\hat n)\cdot\hat n=0\Rightarrow\vec r\cdot\hat n=d\,(\hat n\cdot\hat n)=d$. Cartesian: with $\hat n=l\hat i+m\hat j+n\hat k$ ($l,m,n$ direction cosines) and $\vec r=x\hat i+y\hat j+z\hat k$: $lx+my+nz=d$.
